headline: Markets digest Fed-hike whiplash as oil-yield link tightens
body: This week's action has been a two-step: Wednesday's first Fed rate hike in three years — a quarter-point move to 3.75%-4%, delivered unanimously but paired with Chair Kevin Warsh's warning that inflation has run above target for more than five years — knocked the Dow down over 600 points as 16 of 18 policymakers penciled in at least one more hike this year. Thursday reversed nearly all of it: the Dow gained 316 points to 51,778, the S&P 500 rose 1.1% to 7,638, and the Nasdaq jumped 1.7% to 26,418, led by Nvidia, Amazon and a run in AI-adjacent chip names like Intel and Qualcomm. Friday's futures are essentially flat, with Asian markets extending the bounce overnight, suggesting the market is digesting rather than extending Thursday's relief rally.

The more unusual dynamic underneath this week's swings is the tight coupling between oil and Treasury yields — their rolling correlation has climbed to 0.96, the strongest since 2019 — so Thursday's pullback in crude to around $101 a barrel did double duty, easing both the inflation worry and the yield spike that drove Wednesday's selloff. Retail chatter looks scattered rather than convicted: StockTwits skews modestly bullish on SPY and neutral on QQQ, but the busiest tickers span AI-infrastructure and software names alongside a crypto bid (bitcoin and XRP both higher), with no single meme-stock or panic thread dominating. One clear idiosyncratic mover, Generac, jumped sharply premarket on news of an Amazon warrant deal — a reminder that single-stock catalysts, not broad sentiment, are driving today's more notable moves.
